note: The contract's vocabulary and its values, one file (#630, #634, freeform #629). `tokens`: every token's name, its default value and the axiom or rule it serves; a name is the contract's and ours, a value is a pick and the person's, but for the three marked `fixed` (error, write, live: the meaning channel), whose values no person's AI re-maps. `palette`: the preset values the names are laid from (the functional colours, the gradients, the creature, the scale, the material, the motion), once sol/design/palette.json. tokens.mjs, run by the face's build, writes both from here: sol/mac/src/palette.css and creature/palette.ts from `palette`, sol/mac/src/tokens.css from `tokens`; never written by hand. `contract` is the one number: /health says it, every record is stamped with it. `places` are where a block may render. `migrations` holds one entry per contract bump, { from, to, keys: { old: new } }, a key renamed or, set to null, retired; a step without its entry fails tokens.mjs, and the engine runs them over a person's blocks at the first start after a release (engine/src/release.ts).

The references swap in here; run palette-build.py, no code changes. Functional colours are fixed signals for the states; the seat gradients colour everything at rest, as before step 3 (repair 2026-10-18: only the chat box's highlight goes plain); the creature's ten colours are named for the things that wear one.

sets.note: the palette a person's pieces wear (brand.md, Colour, 2026-11-15, #1237): six shades in the jelly's order. Every set follows one recipe: one brightness band, a shade's strength never the pure hue, neighbouring hues only; so no two can clash. `default` is the brand's own six softened; the rest were taken from the reference pins' own colours (mine/look/brand/colour.html) and are picks, like a ground. curve.why: block 18: a stage block's frame (v4 §4 rule 11, #738; looks.card's take b, between); mark 5: a block kind's 16px mark in its head; box 20: the box in hand (ui.md c-box, #761)

ground.note: the ground (#1183, the board 11-14, the aura-ground family: sol/design/system/ground/pins-aura.jpg). What the pins do, read 2026-11-14: one hue per ground; what varies is lightness, never the colour; the paper carries the hue; the patches are huge, soft, and run off the edges, never a shape sitting in the space; grain over all; the UI small and sharp on it (the ask: calm, never bright, sharp or flamboyant). A take: `paper` (#rrggbb) and `blobs` [colour, x, y, r] in the same hue, lighter or deeper, placed at or past the edges (x, y of the window, r of its width), blurred by `blur`; `goo` [gain, cut] left at [1, 0] so no edge is cut; `grain` per take; `drift` seconds. Drawn by the kit's Ground (sol/mac/src/kit/Ground.tsx). The ground is a background a person picks, not part of the UI (2026-11-14): the set offered is black glass over the desk (today, the default: `pick` glass), mist, cream, dusk; the UI system's language comes from the frame, pills and Sticker walks.

system.note: The one system (#1213, 2026-11-15 02:30: distil each pin family, one system, everything drawn from it). Spine: folders & cards, every piece is an object; joined by chips & pills (the control's edge), stickies & stickers (colour means something), print & zine (the type) and the jelly (its colours and spring). Rules, one line each with its reason: sol/design/system/rules.md. Every accent piece (kit/Accent.tsx) and the body (src/body) draw from these and nothing else. `depth`: the five steps a thing can sit at, each { fill, rim (the lit top edge, on colour), shadow [alpha, y, blur] } on the dark ground; `light` the light ground's fills. `role`: what a colour means, the one ladder (rest grey → picked pearl → Sol's jelly → meaning flat). `shape`: the three outlines. `type`: the roles over scale.type. `move`: each motion as [duration name, easing name] from palette.motion plus its amount.

block.title: A block, as a card
block.note: the block frame as a card (#766, the board 11-14, the folders & cards family). What the pins do, read at full size 2026-11-14: a card is one solid thing, its fill one step off the ground (white or pearl on paper, a charcoal on black), never see-through; one big continuous corner all round; its weight is a wide soft low shadow on paper and a lit top rim on black; the name sits in a tab that steps up out of the body (the folder's lip), joined by one soft curve; states are small marks inside (a dot, a pill, a stamp, a note), the frame itself never recolours; several of the same thing are a stack, sheets peeking above; a card lifted overlaps the others with a bigger shadow and stays solid. `fill` the card's colour on a dark and on a light ground; `sheet` a sheet behind it in a stack, a step toward the ground; `rim` the lit top edge's strength on dark; `shadow` [alpha, y, blur] on each; `lift` what a carried card does. The takes are the lip: tab (the pins' folder), band (the head as a band across the top), plain (no lip). Drawn by the kit's Block (sol/mac/src/kit/Block.tsx).
